thesis: Essent Group (NYSE: ESNT, Bermuda holding company; U.S. private mortgage insurer plus a small reinsurance segment). Q3 2026 10-Q (full text read) and the 2026-11-06 earnings 8-K cover read; the press release exhibit itself was not read. Nine month 2026 net premiums earned 827.5M (+11.7%), total revenues 1,072.9M (+13.1%), net income 524.9M versus 535.0M (-1.9%); diluted EPS 5.71 versus 5.29 (+8.0%) because weighted diluted shares fell 9.2% (91.9M versus 101.2M). Q3 net income 163.4M versus 164.2M. Provision for losses rose to 83.5M in Q3 from 44.9M and to 180.7M in nine months from 93.3M, so the loss ratio on earned premium was 28.7% in Q3 (18.2% a year earlier) and 21.8% in nine months (12.6%). Other underwriting and operating expenses rose 29% in nine months partly with the new reinsurance segment and unearned premium effects. TTM net income is 679.9M (FY2025 689.97M from XBRL 10-K less 534.99M plus 524.89M). Price 64.82 (NYSE close 2026-11-11, two quote publishers). Shares 87,971,999 (cover, 2026-10-31); market cap about 5.70B; about 8.4x TTM net income; equity 5,555.1M at 2026-09-30 so price to book about 1.03x (book value per share about 62.58 on 88.77M balance sheet shares); TTM return on average equity about 12%. Dividend 0.35 per quarter (1.40 annualized, about 2.2%). Nine month buybacks 437.1M plus dividends 95.3M equal 85% of operating cash flow of 628.1M; capex was 2.9M; shares outstanding fell 7.0% since year end. Holding company debt is 500M of 6.25% senior notes due 2029 (interest about 31M a year) and an undrawn 500M revolver to 2029. PMIERs Available Assets 3.7B or 177% of 2.1B required at 2026-09-30, the 2024 Available Asset rule changes became fully effective that date. Risk in force ceded under quota share 11.4B. Investments 6.32B; accumulated other comprehensive loss widened to 359.6M from 152.0M.
counterthesis: The business is earning about 12% on equity with book value essentially equal to price, so the market is not paying for growth; the case rests on credit staying benign. The loss ratio has risen sharply (Q3 28.7% versus 18.2%), management says the 2022 to 2024 vintages are entering peak claim frequency, 30-year mortgage rates remain above 7.3% which limits home sales and cure options, and the 10-Q says losses could change in the near term. Reserve releases are not shown in the extract I read, so the quality of the loss ratio rise (new defaults versus lower favorable development) is unresolved; default counts and cure rates were not retrieved. Net income is flat in absolute terms; EPS growth is entirely a share count decline funded by 437M of buybacks that consume 85% of cash flow with distributions to the holding company dependent on insurer dividend capacity and regulator approval. Accumulated unrealized losses of 360M in investments reduce statutory flexibility if rates rise. NMIH (researched 2026-11-07) shows industry-wide default increases, so the pattern is not company specific. The stock fell 7.6% on 2026-11-06 (68.60 to 63.41) and the cause is not confirmed from documents read. Policy and GSE changes (PMIERs, GSE reform, FHFA pricing) are exogenous risks. A low P/E on a cyclical credit insurer at a near peak earnings period is not evidence of cheapness.
invalidation: Loss ratio above about 35% on a sustained basis, default inventory growth with falling cure rates, PMIERs sufficiency below about 140%, loss of GSE approval or adverse GSE reform, tighter reinsurance terms, or buybacks cut to protect capital. Supportive evidence: stable defaults, continued reserve adequacy and 177% PMIERs sufficiency alongside continued buybacks below book-based intrinsic value.
